title: Job lifecycle states — Long-Running Job Controller (Signature)
description:
Signature edition — an original Signature-authored completion, clearly labeled as Signature work and never presented as public record. The long-running job controller shepherds tasks that outlive a single request — bulk ingests, full reindexes, multi-hour migrations: it tracks their lifecycle from submission through completion, persists progress so crashes resume instead of restart, enforces timeouts and cancellation, and reports status honestly. Long jobs fail in interesting ways; the controller's job is to make every failure boring: visible, resumable, and attributable.

This record documents the job lifecycle states approach: Model jobs as queued, running, paused, failed, cancelled, succeeded — with legal transitions.

demo:
# Long-Running Job Controller demo: checkpointed phases with resume after crash.
import json
STATE={"phase":0,"done":[]}
PHASES=["extract","transform","load"]
def run(state,crash_at=None):
    for i,p in enumerate(PHASES):
        if p in state["done"]: print(p,"already done, skipping"); continue
        print("running",p,"...")
        if crash_at==p: print("CRASH during",p); return dict(state)  # state persisted
        state["done"].append(p)
    state["status"]="succeeded"; return state
s1=run(dict(STATE,phase=0,done=[]),crash_at="transform")
print("resuming after crash...")
s2=run({"done":s1["done"]})
print("final:",s2)
